title: Loop Counters, Boundaries and Off-by-One Errors
learningObjectives: Calculate valid index ranges from array/container size.
Trace inclusive and exclusive loop conditions.
Test zero, one, last-valid and one-past-end cases.

understand.concept: Loop bounds determine iteration count. For an N-element array, indexes are 0..N-1. Strict and inclusive comparisons change the final pass.
understand.whyItMatters: Boundary errors can skip the final item or access beyond valid memory.
understand.explain: Trace first and last values. Compare the loop condition to the valid index range.

examples.title: Valid array indexes
examples.explanation: Indexes are 0, 1, and 2; index 3 would be out of range.

examples.title: Trace increments by two
examples.explanation: Outputs 2, 4, 6; then i is 8 and condition fails.

examples.title: Container bound
examples.explanation: Use size() with strict less-than; use range-based for when no index is needed.

practise.guidedTask: For Loop Counters, Boundaries and Off-by-One Errors, trace each example in a table showing the loop's initial state, condition result, body action, update step, and final state. Identify the termination point and boundary behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ exercise focused on Loop Counters, Boundaries and Off-by-One Errors. Include at least three test cases (typical, boundary and termination/invalid-input case where relevant), trace the loop iterations, and explain why it stops or skips/continues as intended.
hints: Write down the loop's starting state.
Trace the condition before/after each pass according to loop type.
Check that every continuing path progresses toward termination.
Test boundary values and early-exit paths.
Count passes explicitly to catch off-by-one errors.

questions.explanation: Zero-based last index equals size minus one.
Index size is one past valid range.
